title: Love is my vocation (Story of a Soul)
hookLine: searching for her place, Thérèse finds it: in the heart of the church, I will be love
tomorrow: calm inside first, or fix the room first? two old answers.

lines: THE ANSWER'S IN THE WRONG CHAPTER.
cards: Every other post is a plan: the major, the city, the five-year path. Thérèse wants all of them. Warrior, priest, apostle, teacher, martyr.
She wants to preach in every part of the world, until the end of time. And she's a nun inside convent walls. So she opens Paul's letters, looking for her place.
Here's the odd part: she finds it in a chapter that isn't about callings at all.

teach.b: First she reads 1 Corinthians 12, the chapter that should answer her. Paul says the church is one body with many members: apostles, prophets, teachers. It's a list of parts.
She doesn't find herself on it. Not an eye, not a hand. So she keeps reading, past the end of the chapter, and that's the first clue.
Paul says, “covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.” The more excellent way is the next chapter: love. Without it, the greatest gifts are noise.
Second clue: if the church is a body, she reasons, it must have a heart, and that heart burns with love. Love is what moves every member.
Without it, she says, apostles would stop preaching and martyrs would refuse to shed their blood. So the puzzle solves itself. The list names the parts.
She needed what moves all of them. And she writes the words this lesson is named for: my vocation is love. In the heart of the church, my mother, I will be love.
And so, she says, I'll be everything. One more thing to tell a friend: her days didn't change.
Same convent, same work, same sisters.
What changed was where she stood inside them. Paul ends the chapter: “And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.”

how: Readers of Story of a Soul return to this passage when they wonder where they fit; Thérèse read it as a call to live ordinary days with love at the center.

games.q: what does “love is my vocation” mean?
o: a nun's formal vow to stay in one convent for life
Thérèse's discovery that her calling was simply to love
a call to become a missionary preaching abroad

games.q: how she found it — tap the pairs.
p: the King James word for love

s: Thérèse left the convent to follow a bigger calling
she stayed. her days looked the same; where she stood inside them changed.
she found no place for herself on Paul's list of the body's parts
so she kept reading, into the more excellent way.
the King James uses charity for love: Paul's Greek is agape.

games.q: a youth leader reads 1 Corinthians 12 and says, "find your gift on this list." one kid says she isn't on it. what did Thérèse do in that spot?
o: kept reading into chapter 13, and found love, the more excellent way.
picked the gift on the list closest to her and made it fit.
decided she had no gift at all, and stopped looking.
games.why: the list named the parts; she needed what moves them all. in the heart of the church, I will be love.

practice: Choose one place you'll be later today: a desk, a kitchen, a practice, a room with someone who isn't easy. Name what love would look like there, what's most likely to get in the way, and one small move for when it does.
Then rest in that plan for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Love is my vocation. Thérèse's discovery: her calling was to be love, at the heart of the church.

orig.note: Paul's Greek word for love in 1 Corinthians 13, 'charity' in the King James.

carryVoice: Keep this one: I will be love. She didn't change places; she changed where she stood. See you tomorrow.
